The Hydroplant and Reactors' generous electrical supply is regularly overloaded by perforation and other energy-intensive research, but the single greatest threat to the power systems are 'potentivores' - creatures that consume electrical current. GATE's transdimensional studies have, at times, accidentally released several of these entities into the facility, causing rolling blackouts and damage to sensitive apparatus.

Notable among these is IS-0211, which brought the facility to a standstill following its escape from Anteverse 17, in the wake of TransRecon Team 3's second foray to that realm.

Compendium.Title: The Black Fog
Compendium.Subtitle: Weather
SectionTexts:
Little is known about the environmental phenomena associated with IS-0059. Difficult to contain, study has thus far been limited.

These epi-meteorological 'black fog' events are believed to align with manifestations of IS-0059, which are themselves preceded by sightings of insubstantial 'shades'. How these shades communicate or their exact purpose and origin is unknown. Dr. Hammond speculates they are 'materially altered entities, in service of IS-0059', but research is challenging.

While the specific mechanism is unclear, Dr. Hammond has further noted that dissipation of the 'black fog' has, at times, coincided with TransRecon deployment to Anteverse 39.

Compendium.Title: Cold Snap
Compendium.Subtitle: Weather
SectionTexts:
Following exploration of the ultra-frigid Anteverse 67 by TransRecon Team 2, Dr. Kesey reported a curious phenomenon: the area surrounding the perforation equipment was plunged into an 'unmeasurably low temperature state', exceeding anything otherwise achievable in our universe.

This state mirrored the hyper-cryogenic state of A67, and was corroborated by the technical team managing the perforation telemetry. Closure of the portal quickly rectified the situation.

However, Dr. Tengku has speculated that even a small leak could cause immensely cold conditions to supervene throughout the facility for an unknown amount of time. Further, she has demonstrated that the risk of such leaks increases - due to 'entropic pressure buildup' - with every re-entry to Anteverse 67.

Compendium.Title: Fishing
Compendium.Subtitle: Aquatic Life in the Facility and the Field
SectionTexts:
In their exploration of realms far removed from our own, GATE scientists have noted an extraordinary variety of aquatic (but not always water-based) organisms.

While not every fish is immediately recognizable as such, the range of life that has emerged under exceptionally diverse conditions continues to astonish TR teams and field researchers alike.

In order to recover samples of these specimens, personnel have fallen back on age-old techniques.

Fishing is easy enough to get the hang of. With a proper fishing rod equipped, wind up the rod and release it to cast. The longer wind up, the further your cast will be.

Fishing is about focus and patience - you'll need to wait until you get something on the hook, and you shouldn't try and multi-task during this process.

When you have a bite, move about to pull in the opposite direction the fish swims in order to tire it out. When the catch tires, reel it in! Repeat this process until the bobber draws near.

You may not always catch a fish, but you'll generally catch something. Crafting different baits increases the chance of catching certain fish, and can attract their rarer variants. Bait can be added to your rod by holding reload.

As your skills grow, you'll even learn to recognize fishing hotspots, but it takes practice and a keen eye.

Fish can be taken to a proper Chef Counter to be butchered into their constituent parts.

Compendium.Title: Distillations
Compendium.Subtitle: Chemistry Part 1
SectionTexts:
Samples recovered by GATE's dutiful TR teams are often composed of elements and compounds that do not observe the rules of modern chemistry. This prompts GATE researchers to take a more improvisational approach to discovering the properties of these intriguing substances.

Chemistry begins at the Distillation Bench, where you place - usually - organic items into the Input flask (left side). Once an item is in the flask, activating the bench begins the distilling process

After a short period, a Distillation will be produced in the Output flask (right side). The precise output depends entirely on which items were added, and GATE encourages experimentation.

Successful Distillations will be logged in the Distillation section of your GATEPal, including which Distillation resulted, and how many were produced by a given item.

Once you have a Distillation in-hand you may use it to produce a variety of Concoctions at the Chemistry Bench.

Compendium.Title: Concoctions
Compendium.Subtitle: Chemistry Part 2
SectionTexts:
Once at least three Distillations have been successfully created, scientists may combine them at the Chemistry Bench into powerful new items with a variety of - generally - helpful effects.

Place a Distillation into each of the three Input flasks, then activate the bench. After a short time, a Concoction will result. Try experimenting with different inputs and check your GATEPal's Chemistry section for hints from previous research. 

It's important to note that each Input flask can hold up to 8 of the same Distillation at a time, and most chemistry recipes will require more than 1 of a given Distillation to be successful. Unsuccessful combinations will produce an unstable flask, the effects of which when thrown are entirely unpredictable.

Compendium.Title: Taming Pets
Compendium.Subtitle: Friends from Enemies
SectionTexts:
Aggression levels vary across the multitude of fauna samples acquired by TR teams. If subdued through nonlethal means, some of these creatures can be pacified and tamed when hand-fed consistently by a human handler. Earth's humble nacho plate seems particularly effective on most anteverse life, for reasons not yet understood.

Certain items allow our scientists to temporarily capture or pacify entities like IS-0178-A, a.k.a. Pests. Once subdued, they may be tamed by feeding them foods they prefer, creating loyal allies to aid exploration of the GATE Cascade Research Facility. A tamed pet may be picked up, petted, even brought into battle. Some may even produce harvestable items.

A tamed pet will gradually grow stronger when fed a nutritious diet. To feed a tamed pet, use the "Offer" action with any food. If they're hungry, they'll eat it directly out of your hand.

To bring a Companion with you on expedition, utilize the Companion Equip Slot. This harnesses them as a helpful follower in the world, while equipping them with Vital Stabilization Companion Collar. Pets wearing this device will not die if injured, but wait to be picked up and nursed back to health. Only one companion may equipped at a time.

Your companion will grow stronger as you continue to feed it, too. The companion will eat anything, but certain items can produce exciting additional effects.

To keep multiple pets, and ensure they stay safe, consider experimenting with pet beds. Pets are safe from harm while resting in a bed, and those beds are sturdier than they look.

Compendium.Title: Mutating Pets
Compendium.Subtitle: Pet Variations
SectionTexts:
Some creatures known to GATE scientists can undergo rapid mutation when exposed to elements and stimulus outside the norms of their natural environment.

Sometimes, when feeding a pet specific foods you may notice a sparkling effect along with their normal reaction. If you continue feeding that food to your pet, it will mutate into a new form, gaining a new appearance and abilities. Generally, it has been observed that only un-mutated pets can mutate into new forms.

Food is not the only way to mutate a pet: In some cases, an enterprising scientist can combine a pet in their inventory with some gadgets at a crafting bench to create a bionically-enhanced new form.

Compendium.Title: Varsha Patel
Compendium.Subtitle: Materials Engineer
SectionTexts: Patel's engineering talent and acumen were identified and cultivated by a succession of research institutions long before her graduation from the James Franck Institute in 1983.

Patel joined GATE's research staff at Haunch Facility in 1986, before transfering to Cascade at the behest of Sarah Frake in 1987.

Her work in metallurgy and advanced alloys contributed heavily of the success of the Tachyonic Telemetry Targeting Unit project.

Compendium.Title: G.I.S.P. 3.2
Compendium.Subtitle: Gate Immurement Security Protocols
SectionTexts:
Staff in the Security Sector are responsible for producing and promulgating immurement protocols for all GATE Facilities.

The Gate Immurement and Security Protocols, now in its third edition, second revision, are a cornerstone of this authority.

Updated regularly to reflect latest discoveries and best practices, the GISP provisions offer, amongst other things, guidance for all designations of immurement, field work, protective operations and communications.

Compendium.Title: Dr. Mark Kesey
Compendium.Subtitle: TransRecon Chrono-Physicist
SectionTexts: Gone fishin'.

Compendium.Title: Commander Fili
Compendium.Subtitle: 5th Planetary Legion
SectionTexts:
Commander Fili presents as a sentient, indigenous entity living within the simulation that is IS-0083. 

Mourning the loss of her fellows, and the apparent infection of her home by an unknown digital contaminant, Commander Fili has been variously described as a 'convincing simulacrum', a 'cognizant signpost', and 'the unwitting victim of collateral consciousness'.

Compendium.Title: The Waterbot
Compendium.Subtitle: Artificial Life Assistant
SectionTexts:
The so-called 'Waterbot' is an experimental creation of Dr. Stewart Wakeman, dedicated to nurturing nature and tending to the various plants around the GATE Cascade Research Facility.

Whether actually sentient, or a clever simulation, it’s difficult to know for certain, and Dr. Wakeman continues to refuse to contribute to the GATEPal database.

Compendium.Title: Kin Haak Jaal da
Compendium.Subtitle: Exor Chief
SectionTexts: Somewhere between mystic and monster, this creature appears to be a leader of the Exor in this realm, imparting messages that are oblique but unmistakeably warnings.

Compendium.Title: The Unlost
Compendium.Subtitle: Specialist Gatekeeper Unit
SectionTexts: One of the Gatekeeper's most renowned Seer squads, the Unlost are a reconnaissance unit specializing in data and soft target retrieval, under what the GATE Immurement Security Protocols 3.2 term 'non-conventional conditions'.

The Unlost have a reputation for employing wiccan-influenced field tactics and a 'poly-valent' approach to intelligence gathering. As a result, the unit tends to attract recruits unusual even by Gatekeeper standards.

Although most Gatekeepers are accustomed to operating in myriad anteverses with little or no support, the Unlost are distinct for their unconventional approaches to containment, refusing to share their methods with operational staff while scoring highest in GISP Pacified Retention of Immurement Subjects. Their methods have at times caused issues - notably in Anteverses 33, 42 and 171 - however they continue receive significant operational freedom and decision-making flexibility in the field.

Compendium.Title: Dr. K. Hill
Compendium.Subtitle: Plant Supervisor
SectionTexts:
An energetic and generally respected - not to say longstanding - manager of GATE's nuclear engineering team, Dr. Hill is a garrulous exponent of all things atomic. Some might even call him the Plant Supervisor.

For someone who spends as much time as Dr. Hill does knee-deep in nuclear byproducts, whether figuratively or literally, he is renowned about the Facility for his lustrous mane of hair and snappy rapport.

Compendium.Title: Hasta Tria
Compendium.Subtitle: High Inquisitor
SectionTexts:
An extaordinary intellect driven by a penetrating curiosity, High Inquisitor Hasta Tria reached a senior rank within the Order in spite of, or due to, his occasional divergance from accepted orthodoxy. 

While he fears annulment for his actions during the Cassida Cascada, there are few among the Order who more fully embody the precept of 'Exitus acta probat'.

Compendium.Title: A299 A-D
Compendium.Subtitle: The Hive
SectionTexts:
A range of related larval organisms, A299-A, B, C and D are presumed to derive from Anteverse 299, where similar entities were observed on the first - and only - TransRecon expedition to that location. 

Following the destabilization of the GATE Cascade Research Facility's perforation network, the organisms (and a portion of their hive) appear to have intersected an area of the Facility's older and defunct mining region, which was previously solid rock, interspersed with horizontal mineshafts.

While under-researched, the creatures are believed to be a hive entity that communicates largely by scent and olfactory cues. The organisms are also believed to, at some phase in their life-cycle, form the structure of the hive itself.

Their intelligence or otherwise is yet to be determined and will require further research.

Compendium.Title: A299-E
Compendium.Subtitle: Nyth the Gluttonous
SectionTexts:
Previously unknown to GATE, A299-E is an uncontained, gelatinous gastropodal creature believed to originate from Anteverse 299. Recent perforation events have resulted in the entity (and what is presumed to be a section of its hive) manifesting in the defunct mines region of the GATE Cascade Research Facility.

The immense organism appears disoriented. No communication has been attempted, nor close study, but reports note its obsessive pursuit of nourishment, and a curious protruberance from its frontal skull.

Compendium.Title: Anteverse 299
Compendium.Subtitle: The Encroachment
SectionTexts:
Known but unmapped, Anteverse 299 has previously been visited by TransRecon Team 7, who judged the location hostile and requested more probe-based research before further expeditions could safely proceed.

Populated by a plethora of varied larval, troglyditic, cancrine, gelatinous, crystalline, fungal, vermicular and semi-sentient biomechanical entities, Anteverse 299 is a realm to be 'treated with great respect', in the words of Dr. Derek Manse.

Precisely how a significant piece of this realm ended up embedded in the depths of the GATE Cascade Research Facility remains unknown, and the threat of further regional replacements weighs heavily on the minds of many researchers.

Compendium.Title: Nibbles
Compendium.Subtitle: Experimental Subject
SectionTexts: It would seem Dr. Wakeman conducted a test run of his human transference technology by uploading a rat's brain to a small device. The creature, such as it is, appears to still be obsessed with cheese.

Compendium.Title: Jimmy Sanders
Compendium.Subtitle: Taco Guy
SectionTexts:
Like many young New Zealanders in search of warmth and a little adventure, Jimmy moved to Sydney in 1992, where he landed a job at a little-known research facility in the Outback. He should have read the fine print.

Like similar service jobs on large isolated mines, his new role came with long periods on site, and little contact with the outside world, but fantastic pay. Jimmy was familiar with being far from civilization and having few friends. Everything else the job involved, less so.
